decisions.reason: L1 genuinely overstated the equivalent-model case: an arbitrary intertwiner gives S_ik(S^{-1})_lj/d, not two deltas. The character proof only needs inequivalent representatives or the identical chosen model, so restricting the Given and recording both formulas repairs the interface without changing the argument's substance.

Killing each simple-root operator did not by itself license the load-bearing assertion that all of n-plus kills w_i. The repair imports the Serre generator statement and observes that brackets and linear combinations of operators killing w_i also kill it, so the highest-weight nonvanishing argument is now valid.

The common-root-kernel identification was essential and L3 did not expose the adjoint weight decomposition it used. The repair cites the root definition directly, derives that the zero space is the toral algebra from C_G(T)=T, and therefore proves that all root values are one exactly when the adjoint action is trivial.

The original proof applied semisimple Lie-algebra root results before establishing the reductive splitting, Cartan subalgebra, or equality of compact-group and Lie-algebra roots. The repair derives the centralizer equality, splits off the centre, proves the derived torus is Cartan, and differentiates the actual T-weight decomposition before constructing root triples.

The needed group is supplied only by composing three existing interfaces: semisimple realization gives a compact form, covering theory gives its simply connected cover, and the lattice-sandwich theorem proves that cover is compact with character lattice P. L2 now states and cites that composition explicitly; the mathematical classification did not require a new theorem.

The Serre-presentation statement does not provide the locally nilpotent Weyl automorphisms on which positivity of the compact form depended. The repaired proof derives them on the adjoint module from finite-dimensional sl2 theory, verifies the two exponential words agree, proves they commute with compact conjugation, and reduces every root to a simple root by height.

The library's canonical definition explicitly makes a finite-dimensional complex representation of a compact Lie group a continuous homomorphism, and the theorem links that definition through its matrix-coefficient interface. Thus its coefficients are continuous and integrable; discontinuous abstract unitary homomorphisms are outside the stated carrier.

reviews.reason: I checked the general intertwiner formula, the inequivalent case, and the identical-model specialization term by term in the character sum. The revised representative convention makes the two proof cases exhaustive, and the focused precheck and strict proof contract both pass.

I checked PBW injectivity on U(n-minus), the sl2 commutator at exponent m_i+1, generation of n-plus by the simple e_j, and the weight-order exclusion of the original highest weight from every generated submodule. The focused proof checks pass.

I verified the centre as the common root kernel from the full adjoint decomposition, the Smith-normal-form annihilator duality, recovery of both C and X, extension of quotient root-data isomorphisms to P, and reduction from full root-data automorphisms to diagram automorphisms. Conrad and Landesman's Appendix V.2 confirms the marked-lattice correspondence and outer-automorphism quotient.

I checked the reductive splitting, toral centralizer and Cartan argument, differentiation of group weights, negative Killing form, compact-conjugation normalization, SU(2) integration, reflection action, and the regular-torus centralizer proof of surjectivity onto the analytic Weyl group. Etingof's compact-form calculation corroborates the normalization used.

I checked the central-plus-derived finite covering, construction of the simply connected compact semisimple factor with lattice P, finite torus annihilator duality, realization of an abstract root datum, and descent of the integrated Lie-algebra isomorphism through the exact covering kernels. The added adjoint-decomposition citation also licenses centrality in the realization step.

I checked the Serre-algebra real involution, the finite-dimensional sl2 derivation of Weyl automorphisms, positivity of minus the Killing form on every Cartan and root summand, compact integration, the common finite central cover, realization by Aut(k)^0, and invariance under finite central isogeny. Etingof Proposition 39.8 and Theorem 42.4 support the compact-form and simply connected compact-group endpoints.

I traced the theorem's representation terminology to the canonical definition, which includes continuity, then checked the operator-averaging intertwiner argument, the inequivalent and equivalent cases, the trace normalization, and the general change-of-model formula. No edit was mathematically warranted, and all focused checks pass.
